newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Despite claims by Coles Myer's biggest shareholder, Solomon Lew, that he was unaware of the details of the controversial 1990 Yannon deal, the Australian Securities Commission says Lew was aware of "all aspects" of the deal as he was a participant in the transaction. The ASC made its allegation as part of its defence of a case brought by Lew seeking a declaration that the ASC was wrong to release transcripts of his evidence about Yannon. Page 1.

Despite a warning from the ACTU of a full-scale industrial confrontation with the government if the maritime union is punished, the federal government has signalled it will encourage new entrants on the Australian waterfront if shipping companies do not display sufficient commitment to reform. Page 2.

Following a new three-year, A$40 million deal to supply global value added services to Hilton International and similar recent account wins with British Aerospace and Telewest, Telstra expects this week to be awarded an international telecommunications licence in Britain. Page 4.

In an effort to encourage its staff of 191 people to remain loyal while it is being privatised, Axiom Fund Management will pay about A$15 million to staff who stay with Axiom for 60 days after completion of the sale. The payments will be made progressively, with half being paid at the end of the period. Page 21.

According to the September quarter Market Share Report, released on Friday by ASSIRT Investment Research and Technology, BT Funds Management recorded a net inflow of funds of more than A$480 million, placing at the top of the retail funds management industry's inflow tables. BT had the highest net inflow of any of the 85 managers in the survey. Page 21.

Small electricity generaror Pacific Hydro Ltd and its two joint venture partners have signed a A$530 million electricity contract to build a A$185 million hydro electric power station on the island of Luzon and supply electricity to the National Power Corp of the Philippines under a 25-year build, own and transfer agreement. Page 21.

After uncovering four promising diamond mine pipes so far in the Merlin cluster, diamond exploer Australian Exploration Ltd, in which Ashton Mining hlolds 77.6 percent, will look at establishing a major diamond mine at the Merlin site in the Northern Territory. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Pressure for another interest rate cut continues to mount, after the Australian dollwr posted a fresh six year high of US$0.8144 at the weekend, up from $0.8097 on Friday. National Bank managing director Don Argus conceded on Sunday that the rising dollar would trim earnings from the bank's overseas operations and he said he believed there was room for a further 0.5 percent cut in interest rates. Page 29.

As part of its plan to capture half of the Europe-Asia-Pacific corporate telecommunications market, Telstra has signed a A$42 million deal with Hilton International which will see it provide the hotel group with a global telecoms package, includng full domestic and international services at hotels in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as managing arrangements in the Asia-Pacific region. Page 29.

Although the Native Title Tribunal expects negotiations between RTZ-CRA's Century Zinc, the Queensland Government and five local Aboriginal groups over the A$1.1 billion Century Zinc mine in the Queensland Gulf to conclude by about mid-February, complicatons could arise to delay the process as it is believed the claimants have not reached a common position. Page 29.

In its report to the Federal Government, the Companies and Securities Advisory Committee has called for the introduction of whistleblower-style protection for people who voluntarily disclose information under continuous disclosure rules and has recommended the Australian Stock Exchange be given greater legal immunity when it passes on information to the Australian Securities Commission. Page 29.

The Queensland Court of Appeal has ordered FAI Insurances chief executive Rodney Adler to appear at a court inquiry run by a liquidator still pursuing deals done just before the collapse of Christopher Skase's Qintex empire. The deals involved payment of A$5 million to FAI by Skase-controlled company Qintex Group Management Services for insurance policies covering the loss of senior executives. Page 31.

Australia's largest liquor retailer, Liquorland, has announced plans to refurbish more than half the company's 385 outlets during the next two years and expand the network's size to 430 outlets by 2000 as part of an ambitious proposal to raise turnover to A$1 billion before the end of the decade. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Several overseas companies, including the Scottish Rail and U.S. rail giant Amtrak, are believed to have expressed interest in rail group Australian National, with the Federal Government announcing yesterday that it would be privatised. Macquarie Bank, TNT and Brambles are also tipped to show interest in AN, which runs passenger services and the freight lines SA Freight in South Australia and Tasrail. Page 35.

Having taken Brambles Industries into Europe and the United States and overseen the formation of the alliance between British Airways and Qantas, Gary Pemberton ended his 24-year association with the company after securing a position on the board of global mining giant RTZ-CRA, attracted by the prospect of working with a company based in both the United Kingdom and Australia. Page 35.

Despite market expectations that Oil Search will launch a counter takeover bid for Discovery Petroleum that will surpass Premier Oil's A$105 million offer, when Oil Search's board meets today it could hold back from such a move for purely commercial reasos. Page 35.

The Commonwealth Bank has won a three-week battle which allows its solicitor seven days to vet any letters about a dispute between the bank and former customer Greg Malouf before they can be published. Malouf, a director of Davridge Pty Ltd, has been engged in a six-year battle with the bank over a cancelled loan facility that cost him his business. Page 37.

After confirming it had acquired a strategic 10 percent stake in Investment Company of the West, stockbroker J.B. Were said it would keep about 2.1 million of the 3.7 million shares it bought from the Coventry Group and unveiled plans to transform the Investment Company of the West from a Coventry investment vehicle into a broad investor in West Australian equities. Page 37.

Vodafone Group chief executive Sir Gerald Whent said on Friday that Vodafone's Australian arm had performed below expectations in the first half to September 30 because of distribution difficulties and would take another year to become profitable. During the period, Vodafone's local operation forced its biggest service provider, Digicall, into receivership over a A$50 million debt. Page 37.
THE AGE

Melbourne's Howe Leather may suffer from the government's decision to exclude it from A$2 billion in subsidies given to automotive and textile industry exports under an incentive scheme. Trade Minister Tim Fischer said the deal was a victory for jobs, as it prevented threatened U.S.-initiated sanctions against Australian companies, but he was unable to guarantee that jobs at Howe Leather would not be lost. page C1.

The sale of rail group Australian National could raise anywhere between A$100 million and A$500 million for the federal government and several companies have already expressed interest in he group, including the U.K.'s Scottish Rail and U.S. giant Amtrak. Under its rail reform package announced yesterday, the government will sell most of AN's assets, but government-owned track will stay in public hands under the management of a new National Track Authority. Page C1.

In its final draft report on continuous disclosure, the Companies and Securities Advisory Committee says continuous disclosure has improved communications within organisations and gained wide acceptance by shareholders. It recommends the Australian Stock Exchange be given qualified privilege and immunity from liability for breach of confidentiality in all circumstances where it gives the Australian Securities Commission information related to continuous disclosure. Page C3.

Under a scheme announced by Victorian Small Business Minister Louise Asher last week, small business operators will be able to obtain an hour of free consultation from accountants, lawyers and other professionals who make up the Victorian Panel of Professinal advisers. Page C3.

Addressing the inaugural Round Table on Small Business Dispute resolution in Canberra last week, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chairman Allan Fels said self-regulation was the best way to resolve problems between small and large businesses and a new mindset was needed, especially for some large companies and their industry associations. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
